profile.campus: Florida (Flexential's Florida-market data centers, buildings in Jacksonville, Tampa, and Fort Lauderdale)
profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Tampa - West) is located at 9417 Corporate Lake Drive, Tampa, FL 33634. The operator publishes a footprint of 31,600 square feet and 1.81 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HIPAA, ISO 27001, SSAE 18. Duke Energy, a major Florida utility, announced a five-year, $103 billion growth plan in 2026 that it expects to grow further, targeting 20 gigawatts of new generation over the coming decade; the company said AI data center customers including Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Meta were a primary driver alongside population growth of roughly 200,000 people a year into its service territory and grid-hardening investment against severe weather, per Fortune's reporting. Duke CEO Harry Sideris said hyperscale data center customers are paying for their own dedicated infrastructure and that broader rate increases stem mainly from population growth and grid resilience work rather than data centers alone; in Florida specifically, Duke has been replacing wooden utility poles with steel and concrete as part of its storm-hardening strategy. About 60% of Duke's planned capital spending is allocated to new generation (gas turbines, solar, battery storage, and nuclear plant life extensions) and the remaining 40% to grid expansion and upgrades. Duke separately confirmed in 2025 that it was exploring building data centers of its own in Florida, according to WUSF's reporting.

Florida's data center sales-tax landscape changed materially in 2025: House Bill 7031, effective August 1, 2025, eliminated the state's sales-tax exemption on equipment, electricity, and construction materials for data centers with IT loads below 100 megawatts, preserving the exemption only for facilities at or above that threshold, with no grandfather clause for existing sub-100 MW facilities, per Ryan LLC's tax-advisory analysis. All of Flexential's Florida buildings, including this one, operate well under that 100 MW threshold, meaning they and their colocation tenants would no longer qualify for the exemption on new purchases made after the effective date, a shift that has been reported to create potential retroactive tax exposure and pressure toward lease renegotiations for smaller colocation operators statewide.

reading.body:
Flexential Tampa–West is a 31,600 square foot facility at 9417 Corporate Lake Drive with 1.81 MW of critical load UPS capacity. This is the third-largest published capacity among four data centers in Florida with disclosed megawatt figures, representing 19 percent of the state's 9.35 MW of published IT load. The facility ranks within a mapped footprint of 13 data centers across the state, most of which do not publish capacity.

The campus holds certifications for PCI DSS compliance, SOC 1 Type II and SOC 2 Type II audit attestations, HIPAA regulatory coverage, ISO 27001 information security, and SSAE 18 service organization controls. These qualify it for regulated workloads in healthcare, finance, and enterprise IT, though the operator's site does not name which tenants occupy the building.

At a standard density of 40 kW per rack for enterprise colocation, 1.81 MW of IT load corresponds to approximately 45 racks as an assumption. This capacity is too small to anchor enterprise AI training infrastructure, which typically requires hundreds of megawatts per site. The facility sits in a state with minimal published data center capacity and represents the tail of the distribution, not a constraint point on AI scaling.
